correctness.rationale: The exact extension identity is proved by a case analysis for the three relationships to an added maximal parameter and handles the only apparent zero-extension configuration. Independent ideal lower bounds give the sharp chain minimum and strict increment on nonchain remainders. For a chain remainder the exact excess is (k+1)(m-k); for a nonchain remainder the equality equation forces either a unique doubled level or a chain plus isolated point. Standard finite ideal-rank reasoning classifies the J(Q)=m+2 case. Direct independent ideal/filter enumeration verifies all transitive relations through six elements, with no extrapolation from computation.

value.rationale: A natural finite-base model-theoretic invariant has a sharp strict separation from its chain minimum: every deviation costs at least n-1 one-types, and equality is exactly one doubled level or a wholly isolated parameter. The proof classifies all sizes and equality shapes rather than recomputing a small table. The local type change under individual comparability insertions can have either sign, so the global second extremum supplies a mathematically substantive stability boundary not obtainable from naive monotonicity.
